summary: A 104 x 64 x 42 block less a 100 x 60 x 41 cavity open at the bottom (2 mm walls and roof), as in the test (the issue's 100 x 60 x 40 box shelled outward 2 mm). R5 on the outer top edge (y = 32, z = 42, length 104) together with R5 on the concave inner roof/wall edge below it (y = 30, z = 40, length 100) in one fillet was refused as too large (largest 4 mm), although the two built one after the other; #1720 made the fit check count the material the inner round adds. The outer round removes 25(1-pi/4) mm^2 along 104 mm, the inner one adds it along 100 mm: the cavity corner (30, 40) lies 3*sqrt(2) = 4.24 mm from the outer round's ball centre (27, 37), inside its radius, so the removed region stays in material and misses the added one. #1720's test also refused R5 on the outer edge alone; SolidCraft PR #2852 later let it build (it leaves the inner corner 0.76 mm inside the round and reaches it only past 2*sqrt(2)/(sqrt(2)-1) = 6.83 mm), and the test on main builds it. R7 on the outer edge alone breaks through the wall (#2299, tangency-labs/solidcore#2311): with fillet_refuse_rounds_breaking_through it is refused with its fit, and the fit builds. R7 on both edges is not covered. Tolerances are 0.1 % of the outer round's volume. Volumes are closed form.

cases.name: shelled_block
cases.note: Control: 2 mm walls and roof, open bottom, no rounds.

cases.name: round_5_outer_edge_alone
cases.note: R5 on the outer top edge only: refused when #1668 was fixed, builds since SolidCraft PR #2852 (the inner corner stays 0.76 mm inside the round).

cases.name: round_5_both_sides_of_wall
cases.note: #1668: R5 on the outer top edge and the inner roof/wall edge in one fillet call, refused before #1720.

cases.name: round_7_outer_edge_refused_with_its_fit
cases.note: #2299: R7 on the outer top edge alone. The ball centre (25, 35) is sqrt(2)*(7-2) = 7.07 mm from the inner corner (30, 40), so the round breaks through the wall. With the default flags the pinned port returns a self-intersecting body with the whole section removed (WR-707); fillet_refuse_rounds_breaking_through refuses it and reports the largest radius that stays inside the wall, less the fit margin.

refused.error: refused; the largest size that builds

fit_size.source: 2*sqrt(2)/(sqrt(2)-1) - 0.01: the radius at which the round reaches the inner corner (30, 40), less the 0.01 fit margin (tangency-labs/solidcore#2311)

cases.name: round_at_the_fit_builds
cases.note: The fit #2299's refusal reports, 2*sqrt(2)/(sqrt(2)-1) - 0.01, builds on the outer edge: the round stays inside the wall.
